message.content:
Sure! If you’re looking for a machine that can bake a chocolate cake, here are a few options that work well:

| Machine | Why it’s good for baking a chocolate cake | Tips for best results |
|---------|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Conventional oven** | The most common choice. Gives even heat and allows you to control temperature precisely. | Use a springform pan or a round cake pan. Preheat to 350 °F (175 °C). |
| **Convection oven** | Uses a fan to circulate hot air, which can bake the cake more evenly and slightly faster. | Reduce the temperature by about 25 °F (15 °C) compared to a conventional oven. |
| **Toaster oven** | Great for small cakes or cupcakes. Compact and energy‑efficient. | Keep an eye on the timer; toaster ovens can brown quickly. |
| **Smart oven (e.g., June Oven, Tovala)** | Offers precise temperature control and sometimes pre‑set “cake” programs. | Follow the app’s instructions for optimal baking time. |
| **Bread machine with cake setting** | Some bread machines have a “cake” mode that mixes batter and bakes it. | Use the cake setting and a suitable pan that fits inside the machine. |
| **Microwave oven** | Quick for small, single‑serving cakes or mug cakes. | Use microwave‑safe cake pans or paper cups. |
| **Pressure cooker / Instant Pot** | Can bake a cake using the “steam” or “cake” function. | Use a silicone ring or a cake pan that fits inside the pot. |

### Quick Recommendation
If you’re just starting out or want the most reliable results, a **conventional oven** is your best bet. It gives you full control over temperature and baking time, and you can easily adjust for different cake sizes or types. If you already own a convection oven, that’s even better—just remember to lower the temperature a bit.

Happy baking!
